+        prev = idx

+        # last item: the token to mark as never produced when its merge
+        # finds nothing ("" for idx < 256, which the input may contain)
+        app((a + b, c, a, b, c if idx > 255 else ""))
+    return table
+
+
+def _apply_table(s, table):
+    # every merge of the table in order, done in C with str.replace; a merge
+    # whose pair has a token that no earlier merge produced cannot match, so
+    # it is skipped (and its own token is then never produced either)
+    dead = set()
+    add = dead.add
+    for ps, c, a, b, k in table:
+        if a in dead or b in dead:
+            add(k)
+            continue
+        t = s.replace(ps, c)
+        if t is s:
+            add(k)
+        else:
+            s = t
+    return s

actions.reason: I tried skipping merges in the C str.replace merge table when a pair contains a token that no earlier merge produced. Outputs were identical, but encode_ir got worse (ratio 1.0022). That means the replace loop is a negligible part of encode_ir. What's left is mostly fixed cost: interpreter start, importing and compiling the regex module, the harness itself, and findall. I found no safe change within this budget that cuts that by 1%. Swapping regex for stdlib re would risk Unicode category differences.

journal.text:
I tried to cut encode_ir in minbpe/_heap.py. In the C str.replace merge table, I skipped merges whose pair contains a token that no earlier merge produced. I read regex.py, _heap.py, base.py and gpt4.py first, then edited _heap.py several times and trimmed my first 24-line insert down to 8 lines.

The sandbox evaluation was rejected for no_improvement. Outputs were identical and the guard was ok, but encode_ir went from 373964248 to 374802614, ratio 1.0022 against the required 0.9900. train_ir was flat at ratio 1.0000. I gave up and did not submit a candidate.

I now believe the replace loop is a negligible share of encode_ir. Most of the cost looks fixed: interpreter start, importing and compiling the regex module, the harness itself, and findall. Pruning the merge table does not move it.

Next time I should profile what encode_ir actually counts before editing. Then I would look at regex compile and import cost or at findall chunking, rather than the merge loop.
